properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured) 2026-10-30: six /brainstorm rounds in a design that is a member of the dev_reflow2 hub recorded 22 ideas without one search outside that design. The look-first step is advisory and scoped to the one design being written, and nothing at write time reaches the hub
properties.statement:
OBSERVED (claude.ai chat, design 180abbe09345b93d 'reflow2/flo2 10-minute talk', a member of the dev_reflow2 hub since its creation that session): across six /brainstorm rounds (01:15 to 02:15 local), the agent made 22 exploratory add_decision writes and zero search_design calls in any other design. Several ideas were already settled elsewhere in the hub: the three-way partnership is a DesignRule in reflow2, the human-decision-process story was settled 2026-10-12, 'project brain' is the hub page's term. A '40+ MB' figure contradicted the recorded 8.3 MB export. The owner had to ask for verification. NOT AFFECTED: the linking step, which the near-match guard enforces, was done on every write (one refusal, then complied).

CANDIDATES AND MEASUREMENTS. (A) The brainstorm skill's 'look for the answer' step names search_design in the design being written and never mentions a hub or its members. Read in the skill text served that session: CONFIRMED, no hub instruction (contrast root-cause, which says 'search every member'). (B) list_my_designs(hub) said 'Read the hub skill before writing'. The agent never read it until after the failure, and the hub skill section 3 says exactly what was missed: on a server's hub, its address searches every member. CONFIRMED. (C) The agent read the /brainstorm line 'Don't start building or researching any of this yet' as forbidding lookup, and noted that reasoning twice, which conflates step 2 (don't research the idea) with step 1 (look for the answer). CONFIRMED from the session. (D) Nothing at write time signals the hub: plain search_design in the member returns only its own nodes with no mention of the hub; tracked_designs is not served on the hosted server; the near-match guard on add_decision compares within the one design. CONFIRMED. (E) The observation is wrong and the agent did check: REFUTED, zero cross-design searches before 02:17. DECISIVE MEASUREMENT: one search_design through the hub's own design (662c0b99b5d5a913) searched all 28 member designs and returned the accepted partnership DesignRule as the top hit. The capability existed; one call per brainstorm would have found it.

CLASS. A look-before-you-write step that is advisory text, scoped to one design, whose cross-design form lives in a different skill the agent must choose to open, with nothing at write time checking it. The enforced step (linking) was followed every time and the advisory one never, which matches the measured 19-24% skill-opening rate where no tool demands the skill. The 2026-09-28 fix (chg:the-brainstorm-skill-looks-for-the-answer-before-framing-a-question-as-open) was advisory text at the same scope and did not prevent this recurrence in a new form, so it fixed the trigger and not the class.

CANNOT ESTABLISH: whether fixing the skill text (A) alone would have been enough, or whether only a write-time check (D) would have been. The agent cannot be re-run against both. Not checked: whether the same gap exists for capture-intent and jot.

CANDIDATE FIXES, PROPOSED, NOT BUILT, FOR THE OWNER: (1) when a design is a hub member, the near-match guard on add_decision/add_requirement runs through the hub's view and names accepted near-matches in other members; (2) the brainstorm skill's step 1 says 'in a hub, search through the hub's address', and separates 'look for the answer' from 'research the idea'; (3) make_or_change_a_hub's add reply, and start_a_new_design when the design joins a hub, say to search through the hub's address before writing. A pin-the-class test: an exploratory add_decision in a hub member whose subject is accepted in another member gets a reply naming it. It fails today: 22 such replies named nothing.
